target_customer: Aerospace, launch, defense and other complex hardware operators and manufacturers
problem: Launch and test teams ran critical procedures on paper checklists, spreadsheets and documents with no traceability. Epsilon3 offers software to plan, execute and track procedures, tests and manufacturing.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, sold to launch providers, space agencies and defense customers
product_category: Operations software for complex hardware (electronic procedures, MES, test management)

founders.name: Laura Crabtree
founders.background_notes: Former senior missions operations engineer at SpaceX (TechCrunch, March 2021); YC page cites 15+ years of satellite and spacecraft operations and lead trainer for Demo-2 astronauts.

founders.name: Max Mednik
founders.background_notes: Serial entrepreneur; TechCrunch says his last company Epirus raised at least $144.7M (as stated there). Degrees from YC page.

founders.name: Aaron Sullivan
founders.background_notes: Named as chief software engineer by TechCrunch (2021); listed as co-founder on Wellfound and a robotics.press profile, not on the YC page.

competitors.name: First Resonance
competitors.what: Software moving hardware teams from prototyping to production (ION platform)

competitors.name: Prewitt Ridge
competitors.what: Engineering and management tools for hardware teams

technical_complexity.rationale: Web app with real time procedure execution and collaboration during live launches; reliability and later compliance (FedRAMP, ITAR) are the hard parts, not novel research.

defensibility.rationale: Procedures and records accumulate inside the product and compliance certifications (SOC 2, FedRAMP High per company site) raise the bar, but the core workflow is replicable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought it in sources opened; the main rival was spreadsheets and paper.

market_need_then: Launch industry was growing fast in 2021 (TechCrunch cites analyst estimates of more than $18B by 2026) and the founder said the tools she wanted did not exist for launch operations.

branding.name_origin: Laura Crabtree said on a TechCrunch Found podcast interview that the name comes from a planet in the TV series Babylon 5, after a few iterations to find an easily pronounced name.

identity.logo: Wordmark with registered trademark symbol after the name (company site)
identity.visual_style: Bold section headers and uppercase labels
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, reliability focused: 'Software for hardware that can't fail'

branding.brand_signature: Babylon 5 derived name and the Epsilon3 mission control identity
branding.community_and_virality: Founder interviews on TechCrunch Found and Space Insiders podcasts; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable in the space niche with a story-rich name, but narrow awareness outside aerospace.

outcome_analysis: Epsilon3 pairs founders from SpaceX operations with a booming launch market, signed roughly 40 customers by mid 2022 and raised a $15M Series A led by Lux Capital. It later moved from launch procedures into ERP, MES and test software with defense compliance. No Series B was found as of the sources opened, so growth after 2022 is not verified.
notes: TechCrunch March 2021 reports a seed of about $1.8M; a separate January 2022 headline reports a $2.8M seed (robotics.press, Owler/TechCrunch headline). They may be the same round or an extension, so both are recorded. Totals raised vary by aggregator ($17.8M to $19M). Series A year (2022) comes from outlets such as GovConWire; the company post shows only 'June 20'. The no Series B statement rests on a third party profile. Seed amount in the 2022 round was not verified on the primary page.
